standard_prerequisites: disjoint sum of two ordinals as a two-piece concatenation
the reverse lexicographic order on pairs
well-foundedness witnessed by a least element construction
core_obligations: Prove that the disjoint-sum of any two ordinals with the reverse lexicographic order is a well-order
proof_roadmap: Connectedness: within each piece the order is inherited from a well-order and any two elements in different pieces are comparable, so the order is connected
Well-foundedness: for a non-empty subset X take Y, the subfamily of X whose second coordinate is minimal; Y is non-empty since the second coordinates form a finite set of ordinals
The element of Y with smallest first coordinate exists because the first coordinate ranges in an ordinal and Y is non-empty; it is the least element of X
difficulty_reason: A compact two-step least-element construction; the connectedness clause is a one-line observation on the lexicographic order, the well-foundedness half carries the content.
